description.en: The animal resting yoga pose is a restorative posture that folds the body forward over bent legs in a relaxed kneeling stance. The pose releases tension across the lower back, hips, and hamstrings while restoring breath. It is often used between harder poses or as a cool-down.

en: Kneel on the floor with knees slightly apart and toes together.
Sit your hips back onto your heels.
Fold your torso forward over your thighs.
Rest your forehead on the floor or on a folded block.
Let your arms relax forward in front of you or back at your sides.
Allow your shoulders to soften toward the floor.
Breathe slowly and release tension across the back.
Hold the pose for as long as feels good then come back up slowly.
Releases lower back tension
Opens the hips
Stretches the hamstrings
Restorative active rest
Calms the nervous system
Useful between poses

description.en: The assisted single leg press is performed on a leg press machine, using both feet to lift the weight and one foot to lower it (or vice versa) for assisted single-leg training. The technique allows you to overload the working leg beyond what it could handle alone. It is excellent for building unilateral leg strength.

en: Sit on a leg press machine with both feet on the platform.
Position your feet hip-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety stops.
Press the platform up to full extension with both legs.
Place one foot off the platform.
Lower the platform slowly with just the working leg.
When you reach the bottom, place both feet back on to press up.
Complete reps on one side before switching legs.
Eccentric overload on one leg
Builds single-leg strength
Useful for fixing imbalances
Allows heavier loading than true single-leg
Builds quad and glute size
Reduces injury risk

description.en: The band alternate incline chest press with twist is a unilateral incline press done with a band anchored low. The lifter alternates arms and twists the torso into each press. It builds the upper chest, shoulders, and obliques.

en: Anchor a resistance band at floor level behind you.
Grip a band handle in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance.
Bring the handles to the chest.
Press one handle up at an incline angle.
Twist the torso into the press.
Lower with control and press the other side.
Continue alternating sides.
Trains the upper chest
Adds rotation
Strong band variation
Useful for travel
Builds the obliques

description.en: The band assisted muscle up uses a resistance band looped over a pull up bar with the foot or knee resting in the band loop. The band helps the lifter through the toughest part of a muscle up where the body transitions over the bar. It is a great progression toward an unassisted muscle up.

en: Loop a resistance band over a pull up bar so it hangs down.
Step or kneel into the band loop with one foot or knee.
Reach up and grip the bar with hands shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and pull yourself up explosively.
Drive the chest up to the bar and continue pulling over.
Use the band assistance to transition through to the dip position.
Press up to lockout above the bar.
Lower with control back to the hang.
Trains the muscle up motion
Useful pull up progression
Builds the transition phase
Adjustable assistance
Strong upper body builder
Excellent calisthenics drill

description.en: The band bent over wide grip row is a wide grip row using a resistance band. The lifter stands on the band with feet wide and grips it with a wide overhand grip, then bends over and rows. The wide grip biases the upper back and rear delts.

en: Stand on a resistance band with feet at shoulder width.
Grip the band with both hands wider than shoulder width.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back.
Brace your core and let the band hang at arms length.
Pinch the shoulder blades together.
Row the hands up wide with elbows flared out.
Drive the elbows back at shoulder height.
Squeeze the upper back. Lower with control.
Strong upper back builder
Trains the rear delts
No machine needed
Useful at-home back move
Strong band move
Builds back thickness

description.en: The band horizontal biceps curl uses a resistance band anchored to the side at chest height. Standing perpendicular to the anchor, you curl the band across your body horizontally. The horizontal pull and across-body angle hits the bicep with strong peak contraction and a different stimulus than vertical curls.

en: Anchor a resistance band to a chest-height anchor on your right side.
Stand perpendicular to the anchor with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the band end with your left hand.
Step away from the anchor to create band tension.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Curl the band across your body to your right shoulder by bending the elbow.
Squeeze the bicep hard at the peak contraction.
Slowly extend back to the starting position. Switch sides.
Different angle than vertical curls
Strong peak bicep contraction
Constant band tension through the range
Hits short head of biceps
Useful for breaking through curl plateaus
Easy to scale by changing band tension

description.en: The band lying hip internal rotation is a hip rotator drill done with a band around the knees. The mover lies on the side and rotates the top foot toward the floor against band tension. It builds hip stability and internal rotation.

en: Loop a resistance band around the knees.
Lie on one side with the knees bent at ninety degrees.
Stack the hips and shoulders.
Brace your core and keep the knees together.
Lift the top foot up while keeping the knees stacked.
Hold the position against the band tension.
Lower with control to the start.
Finish all reps then switch sides.
Trains hip internal rotation
Builds hip stability
Strong rotator drill
Useful warm-up
Builds the glutes

description.en: The barbell one-arm side deadlift (suitcase deadlift) is a unilateral deadlift where you grip a barbell at your side with one hand and deadlift it. The asymmetric load creates extreme anti-lateral flexion demand on the core — your body fights to stay upright against the side-loaded weight.

en: Stand next to a barbell positioned on the floor to your right side. Feet hip-width apart.
Squat down and grip the center of the barbell with your right hand.
Brace your core extremely hard. Maintain a perfectly upright torso.
Deadlift the bar by extending your hips and knees.
Stand tall with the bar hanging at your right side — like holding a suitcase.
Do not lean to the right. The core demand is resisting the lateral pull.
Lower under control. Complete reps, then switch sides.
Use moderate weight — the limiting factor is core stability, not leg strength.
Extreme anti-lateral flexion core demand
Builds oblique and quadratus lumborum strength
Develops grip strength under asymmetric load
Exposes left-right core imbalances
Unique deadlift variation
Builds functional carrying strength

description.en: The barbell single-leg split squat is a stationary split squat (Bulgarian-style or standard) performed with a barbell across the upper back. It is essentially the same as the barbell split squat — a stationary lunge variation that builds single-leg strength with heavy bilateral barbell loading.

en: Set a barbell across your upper traps. Unrack and step back.
Step your right foot back into a split stance two to three feet behind you.
This is your fixed position for the set.
Lower your right knee toward the floor by bending both knees.
Descend until your right knee is just above the floor.
Drive through your front (left) foot to return to the top of the split stance.
Complete reps, then switch which foot is forward.
Use moderate weight. Aim for 8 to 10 reps per leg.
Builds single-leg strength with barbell loading
Stationary position allows focused loading
Exposes left-right imbalances
Easier to balance than walking lunges
Easy to load progressively
Useful single-leg accessory

description.en: The barbell standing shoulder pin press is an overhead press variation where the bar starts from pins set at shoulder height in a power rack. Each rep begins from a complete dead stop, eliminating the stretch reflex and bounce. It builds raw concentric strength out of the bottom of the press.

en: Set safety pins in a power rack at shoulder height when standing.
Set up a barbell on the pins.
Step under the bar and grip it slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Position the bar against your front shoulders.
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes.
From the dead-stop position on the pins, press the bar straight up overhead.
Lock out at the top, then lower back to the pins. Reset before the next rep.
Builds dead-stop press strength
Eliminates stretch reflex
Trains the press from its weakest position
Useful for breaking through press sticking points
Forces strict bracing
Strong carryover to overhead press

description.en: The barbell sumo squat is a back-loaded squat performed with a much wider stance and toes turned out at roughly 45 degrees. The wide foot position emphasizes the adductors (inner thighs) and gluteus medius, and tends to be more upright and knee-friendly than a standard back squat. It is a popular accessory lift for building the glutes and inner thighs.

en: Set the barbell in a power rack at upper-chest height. Step under the bar and rack it across your upper traps.
Unrack the bar with a slight knee bend, take two to three steps back, and set up in a wide sumo stance — feet 1.5 to 2 times shoulder-width apart.
Turn your toes out to roughly 30 to 45 degrees. Your knees should track in line with your toes throughout the lift.
Brace your core hard and take a deep breath. Lift your chest tall.
Sit straight down by pushing your knees out toward your toes and bending at the hips and knees together.
Descend until your hip crease drops below the top of your knees (parallel or deeper).
Drive through your full foot, push your knees out, and stand back up. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, then carefully rack the bar.
Emphasizes the adductors and inner thighs more than a standard squat
Heavily recruits the glutes through the wide hip-abducted position
Often more upright and knee-friendly than a standard back squat
Improves hip mobility and adductor flexibility through the deep squat range
Builds carryover strength to the sumo deadlift and wide-stance lifts
Easy to scale by adjusting stance width and load

description.en: The bent arms chin-up hold pulls up to the top of a chin-up and holds the bent-arm position with chin above the bar. The isometric hold builds biceps and lat strength and endurance. It is a useful tool for building chin-up strength and breaking through plateaus.

en: Stand under a chin-up bar.
Reach up and grab the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Pull yourself up so your chin is above the bar.
Hold the top position with elbows bent and chest near the bar.
Brace your core and keep your legs together.
Hold for as long as possible.
Lower yourself slowly back to a hang.
Drop off when control is lost.
Builds biceps endurance
Strengthens the lats
Improves chin-up strength
Useful for breaking plateaus
Develops grip endurance
Bodyweight strength builder

description.en: Bird of paradise pose, or Svarga Dvijasana, is an advanced standing yoga balance. From a bound side angle, you stand up while extending one leg out to the side with the arms bound around it.

en: Stand with the feet wide and turn the right foot out.
Bend the right knee into a side angle pose.
Reach the right arm under the right thigh and the left arm behind the back.
Clasp the hands together for the bind.
Shift weight onto the left foot.
Slowly stand up keeping the bind.
Extend the right leg out and up to the side.
Hold the pose for the desired duration then switch sides.
Builds single leg balance.
Stretches the hamstrings and hips.
Opens the chest and shoulders through the bind.
Calms the mind in classical yoga practice.
No equipment needed.
Improves total body coordination.

description.en: The boxer shuffle is a cardio and footwork drill where you bounce lightly on the balls of your feet in a relaxed athletic stance, alternating which foot bears slightly more weight. It mimics the constant footwork of a boxer in the ring. It builds cardiovascular conditioning, foot speed, and ankle endurance.

en: Stand in a boxer’s stance — feet roughly shoulder-width apart, weight on the balls of your feet, knees slightly bent.
Hold your hands up in a guard position near your face.
Begin bouncing lightly on the balls of your feet, alternating which foot is “lighter.”
Keep the bouncing small and quick — feet barely leave the ground.
Stay relaxed in the upper body. Bouncing should feel rhythmic and effortless.
Maintain the boxer’s stance throughout — do not stand fully upright.
Continue for the desired duration (1 to 3 minute rounds).
Add jab/cross punches for added intensity and engagement.
Builds cardiovascular conditioning
Develops foot speed and rhythm
Improves calf and ankle endurance
Mimics combat sport conditioning
No equipment needed
Engaging and fun

description.en: The cable one arm press on exercise ball combines a single arm cable press with a stability ball base. The lifter lies back on a stability ball and presses a cable handle from chest to lockout. The unstable ball and unilateral load force a brutal core challenge.

en: Set a cable to chest height behind the ball position.
Sit on a stability ball and walk the feet out so the upper back rests on the ball.
Grip a single handle in one hand at the chest.
Brace your core hard and keep the hips lifted.
Press the handle straight up to lockout.
Squeeze the chest at full extension.
Lower with control to the start.
Complete reps and switch hands.
Strong unilateral chest move
Adds core challenge
Trains the obliques
Constant cable tension
Strong cable move
Builds chest size

description.en: The cable seated rear lateral raise is a rear deltoid isolation exercise performed seated on a bench between two low cable pulleys. You cross the cables (right hand holds left cable, left hand holds right) and raise them out to the sides in a reverse fly arc.

en: Set two cables to the lowest position. Attach D-handles.
Sit on a bench between the cables. Cross the cables — right hand grips left cable, left hand grips right.
Start with arms crossed in front of your body at knee level.
Raise both handles out to the sides in a reverse fly arc, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your rear delts at the top.
Lower under control.
Maintain slight elbow bend throughout.
Use light to moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
Seated rear delt isolation with crossed cables
Constant cable tension throughout the arc
Eliminates body english
Easy to load progressively
Builds rear delt size and shoulder balance
Unique cable crossing pattern

description.en: The cable standing wrist roll is a forearm-focused exercise where you roll the rope up by alternating wrist flexions while standing in front of a cable pulley. The cable provides constant tension throughout the roll. It is a brutal grip and forearm builder used by climbers, grapplers, and lifters chasing thicker forearms.

en: Attach a single rope handle to a high or mid cable pulley.
Stand in front of the cable with arms extended in front of you.
Grab the rope with both hands, palms down.
Keep your arms straight and elbows locked.
Roll the rope up by alternating wrist flexions.
Continue rolling until the rope is fully wound up.
Reverse the motion to roll the rope back down with control.
Repeat for time or for a set number of full rolls.
Builds forearm strength
Improves grip endurance
Constant cable tension throughout
Useful for climbing and grappling sports
Strengthens the wrist flexors and extensors
Builds thicker forearms

description.en: The cheat curl intentionally uses body english and momentum to curl a heavier weight (or perform bodyweight curls) past the sticking point, then controls the weight slowly on the lowering (eccentric) phase. The value is in the heavy eccentric loading.

en: Stand with a loaded barbell or heavy dumbbells. Use weight heavier than you can strict-curl.
Use a slight lean-back and hip drive to swing the weight past the sticking point.
Curl the weight to the top position using momentum.
Once at the top, slow down and control the eccentric — lower over 3 to 4 seconds.
The value is the heavy eccentric phase, not the concentric cheat.
Use sparingly — not every set should be cheat curls.
Aim for 5 to 8 reps with heavy eccentric focus.
This is an advanced technique for experienced lifters.
Allows heavier eccentric loading
Builds bicep strength beyond strict curl capacity
Advanced overloading technique
Develops eccentric bicep strength
Used by bodybuilders for advanced arm training
Should be used sparingly

description.en: The dumbbell bench dip with legs elevated places the hands on one bench, the feet on another, and a dumbbell across the lap for added resistance. The elevated legs increase the difficulty and the dumbbell loads the triceps hard. It is a brutal triceps mass builder.

en: Place two benches parallel to each other.
Sit on one bench with hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Place your feet on the second bench with legs straight.
Have a partner place a dumbbell across your hips/lap.
Brace your core and lift your hips off the bench.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor.
Continue until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press through your hands to drive back up.
Builds triceps mass
Loads triceps with weight
Elevated legs increase difficulty
Stronger than bodyweight dip
Useful for arm size
Strong triceps hypertrophy move

description.en: The dumbbell bent arm lateral raise is a lateral raise variation performed with the elbows bent at about 90 degrees throughout. The shorter lever arm allows heavier loading and reduces stress on the shoulder joint. The bent arm position changes the strength curve while still building the side delts.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees with forearms parallel to the floor.
Position the dumbbells in front of your body with palms facing each other.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Maintain the bent arm position throughout.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides by lifting the elbows.
Continue until your upper arms are level with your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back down with control to the starting position.
Allows heavier loading
Reduces shoulder joint strain
Builds side delt size
Different strength curve than straight-arm raises
Useful for breaking through plateau
Strong side delt activation

description.en: The dumbbell front plank arm raise combines a high plank position with a single-arm front raise. Lifting one dumbbell forward while holding the plank challenges your core to resist rotation and your shoulder to stabilize the body on three points of contact.

en: Place two light dumbbells on the floor about shoulder-width apart.
Get into a high plank position with your hands gripping the dumbbells.
Set your feet wider than your hips for stability.
Brace your core hard. Keep your hips square to the floor.
Shift your weight slightly to your left arm and lift the right dumbbell forward to shoulder height.
Hold for one count at the top, keeping your hips level. Do not let them rotate.
Lower the dumbbell back to the floor with control. Repeat on the other side.
Alternate sides for 8 to 12 total reps.
Builds core anti-rotation strength
Develops single-arm shoulder stability
Trains the body to resist hip dropping and rotation
Combines pressing and core work in one efficient movement
Excellent for athletes who need rotational stability
No need for heavy weight to be challenging

description.en: The dumbbell lying femoral is a floor-based hamstring exercise where you lie face down on the floor with a dumbbell held between your feet. Curling the dumbbell up toward your glutes by flexing the knees works the hamstrings without a leg curl machine. It is a strong choice for home training.

en: Place a dumbbell on the floor.
Lie face down on the floor with your feet on either side of the dumbbell.
Squeeze your feet together to grip the dumbbell vertically between your ankles.
Position your arms folded under your forehead for support.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes lightly to keep your hips down.
Curl the dumbbell up by flexing your knees toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top.
Lower the dumbbell back down with control.
Trains hamstrings without a machine
Floor-based, no bench required
Strong eccentric load on the lowering
Easy to scale by changing dumbbell weight
Useful for home training
Develops grip strength in the feet

description.en: The dumbbell one arm floor fly performs the dumbbell fly one arm at a time while lying on the floor. The floor stops the dumbbell from descending too far, protecting the shoulders during the stretch. The single-arm pattern corrects pec imbalances and adds anti-rotation core work.

en: Lie on your back on the floor with a single dumbbell in your right hand.
Press the dumbbell up over your chest with arm extended.
Place your left hand on your chest or at your side.
Maintain a slight bend in the working elbow.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc.
Continue until your upper arm touches the floor.
Pause briefly with the arm on the floor.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbell back over your chest. Switch arms.
Floor protects the shoulders
Strong unilateral chest isolation
Corrects pec imbalances
Adds core anti-rotation challenge
No bench required
Useful for home or travel training

description.en: The dumbbell one arm triceps extension on stability ball is a unilateral triceps drill done bridged on a stability ball. Working one arm at a time loads the triceps long head while the core fights rotation.

en: Sit on a stability ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Walk the feet out and bridge the upper back onto the ball.
Press the hips up so the torso is parallel to the floor.
Hold the dumbbell over the chest with the working arm extended.
Brace the core and keep the elbow pointing up.
Lower the dumbbell back behind the head by bending the elbow.
Press the dumbbell back up by extending the elbow.
Continue for all reps then switch sides.
Isolates the triceps long head.
Trains anti-rotation core.
Ball adds instability.
Builds the back of the arm.
Useful triceps accessory.

description.en: The dumbbell standing one arm extension performs the overhead tricep extension one arm at a time from a standing position. The single-arm load isolates each tricep individually and corrects strength imbalances. The overhead position emphasizes the long head of the triceps with a strong stretch.

en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a single dumbbell in your right hand pressed overhead.
Position the dumbbell directly overhead with arm fully extended.
Place your left hand on your hip or at your side.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Bend your right elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Continue until you feel a strong stretch in the tricep.
Press the dumbbell back overhead by extending the elbow. Switch arms.
Strict single-arm tricep isolation
Strong long head emphasis
Corrects tricep strength imbalances
Builds tricep size
Strong stretch at the bottom
Useful for tricep specialization

description.en: The dumbbell straight arm twisting sit up is a weighted sit-up where the dumbbell is held with straight arms overhead. At the top of each sit-up the torso twists to one side to bring the dumbbell across the body. The combination targets the rectus abdominis and obliques together.

en: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands and press it straight overhead.
Keep your arms long and locked out throughout.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Sit up by curling your torso off the floor.
At the top, twist the torso to bring the dumbbell across to one side.
Twist back through center and lower with control to the start.
Alternate the twist side on each rep.
Loaded core challenge
Hits abs and obliques
Builds trunk power
Trains rotational core
Improves bracing
Brutal ab finisher

description.en: Elbow to knee twists are a standing core and cardio drill where you twist to bring an elbow to the opposite knee. The repeated rotation hits the obliques while keeping the heart rate up.

en: Stand tall with feet shoulder width apart and hands behind your head.
Keep the elbows wide and the core braced.
Lift your right knee toward your chest while twisting your torso left.
Bring your left elbow down to meet the right knee.
Return to the standing start with control.
Repeat on the opposite side, bringing the right elbow to the left knee.
Stay light on your feet and keep a steady rhythm.
Continue alternating sides for the desired duration.
Strengthens the obliques through controlled rotation.
Engages the hip flexors with each knee lift.
Elevates heart rate for cardio benefit.
Improves coordination between upper and lower body.
No equipment needed and minimal space required.
Adds rotational core training to standard cardio.

description.en: The EZ bar 21s is a classic bicep finisher made famous in old-school bodybuilding. The protocol calls for seven bottom-half curls, seven top-half curls, then seven full-range curls, all without rest. The combination of partial ranges and full reps creates an extreme pump and total bicep fatigue.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an underhand grip.
Grip the bar at the inner curves of the EZ bar.
Stand tall with elbows tucked at your sides.
Curl the bar from full extension up to the halfway point only. Repeat for seven half curls.
Without rest, curl the bar from the halfway point up to the top. Repeat for seven top-half curls.
Without rest, perform seven full range curls from full extension to the top.
Maintain elbow position throughout the entire sequence.
Lower the bar back to the starting position with control after the final rep.
Classic bicep burnout finisher
Hits multiple ranges in one set
Creates an extreme bicep pump
Builds bicep size with high time under tension
EZ bar reduces wrist strain compared to straight bar
Useful for breaking through bicep plateaus

description.en: The front toe touching is a fundamental forward fold stretch where the lifter stands tall and folds forward to reach toward the toes. The pose stretches the hamstrings, calves, and lower back. It is one of the most basic stretches and a key warm-up move.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core lightly.
Keep a soft bend in the knees if needed.
Hinge at the hips to fold the torso forward.
Reach your hands down toward the toes.
Allow the head to hang relaxed.
Feel the stretch through the hamstrings and back.
Hold then slowly roll back up.
Stretches the hamstrings
Releases lower back tension
No equipment needed
Easy basic stretch
Useful warm-up move
Strong fundamental stretch

description.en: The impossible dip is an advanced calisthenics skill where you start hanging below a straight bar and pull yourself up and over into a dip position above the bar in one smooth transition — essentially a muscle-up performed extremely slowly and controlled on a straight bar.

en: Hang from a straight bar with an overhand grip.
Pull yourself up (like a pull-up).
As your chest reaches the bar, lean forward and transition your body over the bar.
Push down into a dip position above the bar.
Lower back below the bar in a controlled reverse of the movement.
The transition from below to above is the “impossible” part.
This requires significant pulling and pushing strength.
Master muscle-ups before attempting. Aim for 1 to 3 reps.
Advanced calisthenics skill
Combines pulling and pushing in one movement
Builds transition strength
Develops full upper-body control
Impressive demonstration of strength
Progression from muscle-ups

description.en: The jumping single leg lunge is a single-leg explosive move where the lifter starts in a deep lunge and jumps up off the front leg, landing back on the same leg. The same-leg landing builds serious power, balance, and conditioning.

en: Start in a deep lunge with one foot forward and the back knee near the floor.
Set your front foot flat with knee tracking over the toe.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Drive through the front foot to jump straight up.
Bring the back leg up under you in the air.
Land softly back on the same front foot in a lunge.
Sink back down into the deep lunge position.
Complete reps on one side before switching legs.
Builds explosive single-leg power
Trains balance and stability
Strong conditioning effect
No equipment needed
Useful for athletes
Improves jump strength

description.en: The kettlebell alternating press holds two kettlebells in the front rack and alternates pressing one overhead at a time. The alternating pattern keeps one shoulder working while the other recovers in the rack, extending total time under tension. It also builds anti-lateral flexion core strength as you stabilize against the asymmetric load.

en: Clean two kettlebells to the front rack position.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Brace your core.
Press the right kettlebell overhead to lockout while keeping the left in the rack.
Lower the right KB to the rack.
Press the left kettlebell overhead while the right rests in the rack.
Continue alternating for the desired reps.
Maintain an upright torso throughout. Do not lean away from the pressing side.
Aim for 6 to 10 reps per arm.
Builds shoulder endurance through alternating pattern
Develops anti-lateral flexion core strength
Exposes left-right pressing imbalances
Extended time under tension
Useful for conditioning
Foundational kettlebell pressing variation

description.en: The kettlebell clean and press is a foundational full-body exercise where you clean a kettlebell from the floor (or hang) up to the front rack position, then press it overhead. The combined movement builds power, total-body strength, and conditioning. It is the most versatile single-kettlebell exercise.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Squat down and grip the kettlebell with your right hand.
Drive through your feet and explode upward, swinging the kettlebell up and rotating your wrist around to land it in the front rack position (resting on your forearm at shoulder height).
Stand tall in the front rack. Brace your core hard.
Press the kettlebell straight up overhead by extending at the elbow.
Lock out at the top with arm fully extended above your shoulder.
Lower the kettlebell back to the front rack, then back to the floor or hold for the next rep.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
Builds full-body power and strength
Combines clean and press in one movement
Excellent metabolic conditioning
Develops shoulder stability under load
Time-efficient compound exercise
Foundational kettlebell exercise

description.en: The kettlebell deadlift is a hip-hinge exercise performed with a single kettlebell on the floor between your feet. It teaches the same hip-hinge pattern as the barbell deadlift but with lighter loading and a more forgiving setup, making it the ideal first deadlift variation for beginners and a foundational drill for anyone learning the kettlebell swing.

en: Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet, with the handle aligned with your mid-foot.
Stand with feet just wider than shoulder-width and toes pointed slightly outward.
Push your hips back, bend your knees slightly, and reach down to grip the kettlebell handle with both hands using an overhand grip.
Lift your chest, pull your shoulders back and down, and brace your core. Your back should be flat with a slight natural arch.
Take a deep breath, then drive your feet through the floor and stand up tall, lifting the kettlebell straight up between your legs.
Lock out at the top by squeezing your glutes — your body should form a straight standing line.
Reverse the movement by hinging at the hips first, then bending the knees once the kettlebell passes them.
Set the kettlebell back on the floor between your feet under control. Reset and repeat.
Teaches the hip-hinge pattern with light, forgiving loading
Builds the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back without the spinal load of a barbell
Foundational drill before learning the kettlebell swing
Trains grip strength through the loaded hold
Highly portable — needs only one kettlebell and a small space
Excellent rehabilitation and warm-up exercise

description.en: The kneeling T spine mobility is a thoracic spine rotation drill done from a kneeling position. The mover rotates the upper back from one side to the other while keeping the hips square. It is useful for posture and rotation.

en: Kneel on a soft mat with the hips down on the heels.
Place one hand behind the head with the elbow flared.
Place the other hand on the floor in front.
Brace your core and keep the hips square.
Rotate the upper back to bring the elbow toward the ceiling.
Open the chest and follow the elbow with the eyes.
Reverse the rotation to bring the elbow toward the opposite hand.
Finish all reps then switch sides.
Improves T spine mobility
Strong upper back drill
Useful warm-up
Builds thoracic rotation
Useful for posture

description.en: The landmine one arm bent over row is a popular unilateral back exercise. The barbell anchored in a landmine creates a natural arc that loads the lats and mid back through a smooth pulling path.

en: Anchor a barbell in a landmine and load the working end with weight.
Stand straddling the bar with feet shoulder width apart.
Grip the end of the bar with one hand using a neutral grip.
Hinge at the hips into a strong bent over position with a flat back.
Place the free hand on your knee or hip for support.
Brace the core and pull the bar up toward your hip.
Drive the elbow back and squeeze the lat at the top.
Lower the bar slowly back to full extension and repeat all reps then switch.
Builds back thickness through the landmine arc.
Hits the lats, rhomboids, and rear deltoids.
Trains anti rotation as the body resists the bar pull.
Easy to scale with bumper plates of any size.
Develops grip and biceps strength.
Carryover to bent over barbell rows and deadlifts.

description.en: The lateral walk push-up combines a push-up with sideways shuffle steps. After each push-up, the hands and feet shuffle one or two steps to the side before the next rep. The lateral movement adds shoulder stability and conditioning demands to the basic push-up.

en: Get into a push-up position with hands under shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up to the top of the push-up.
Walk one hand and the same-side foot to the side.
Bring the other hand and foot to meet them.
Perform another push-up.
Continue walking sideways with each rep.
Combines chest and conditioning
Builds shoulder stability
No equipment required
Strong calorie burner
Useful for full-body workouts
Adds variety to push-ups

description.en: The leg up hamstring stretch is a passive supine hamstring stretch where you lie on your back near a doorframe or wall and rest one leg vertically against it (or use a strap to hold the leg up). The position allows gravity and time to deepen the stretch without active effort, making it one of the gentlest hamstring stretches.

en: Lie on your back next to a doorframe or wall corner with your right hip aligned to the wall edge.
Extend your right leg straight up the wall or doorframe. Your leg should be vertical.
Keep your left leg extended through the doorway or along the floor.
Press your right heel into the wall to engage the leg slightly.
Adjust your distance from the wall to control the stretch intensity.
Hold for 30 seconds to 2 minutes. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch.
Switch sides and repeat.
Alternative: lie on the floor and use a strap looped around your foot to hold the leg up.
Passive hamstring stretch — gentle and effective
Allows long holds without active effort
Adjustable depth based on distance from wall
Excellent for tight hamstrings
Calming and restorative
Works at home with just a wall

description.en: The low lunge yoga pose Anjaneyasana I is a foundational yoga pose that opens the hip flexors. The mover drops into a lunge with the back knee on the floor and reaches the arms overhead. It is useful for hip mobility.

en: Step one foot forward into a lunge stance.
Lower the back knee to the floor.
Set the front shin near vertical.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Press the hips forward to deepen the stretch.
Reach the arms straight up overhead.
Look up toward the hands.
Hold the pose then switch sides.
Opens the hip flexors
Stretches the quads
Strong yoga pose
Useful warm-up
Builds hip mobility

description.en: The lever one arm side chest press is a unilateral chest press performed sideways to the machine. The lifter sits with one shoulder facing the machine and presses one arm at a time. The angled position changes the press pattern and adds chest stretch.

en: Sit on a lever chest press machine sideways to one side.
Set the seat so the handle is at chest height.
Grip the handle with the hand closest to the machine.
Brace your core and keep the chest tall.
Press the handle forward and across the body.
Squeeze the chest hard at full extension.
Pause briefly at lockout.
Return with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Strong unilateral chest builder
Constant lever resistance
Adds chest stretch
Builds chest size
Strong machine move
Trains the obliques

description.en: The lever t-bar reverse grip row uses a t-bar row machine with a supinated underhand grip. The lifter grips the close handles with palms up and rows the bar to the belly. The reverse grip pulls the elbows tight against the body and biases the lower lats and biceps.

en: Set up a t-bar row machine with a close grip handle.
Step over the bar and grip the handles with palms facing up.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back.
Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blades.
Set the chest against the chest pad if available.
Pull the bar up to the belly button by driving the elbows back.
Squeeze the lats and biceps hard at the top.
Lower with control to arms extended.
Strong lat builder
Reverse grip biases biceps
Heavy load capacity
Builds back thickness
Useful back move
Strong machine move

description.en: The push up with knee drive combines a push up with a mountain climber knee drive. The lifter performs a push up and at the bottom drives one knee toward the chest. The combo trains the chest, core, and hip flexors in one rep.

en: Begin in a high plank position with hands under the shoulders.
Set the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core hard.
Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows.
At the bottom drive one knee toward the chest.
Return the foot to the start.
Press back up to lockout.
Repeat with the other knee on the next rep.
Combo chest and core builder
Trains hip flexors
Builds shoulder stability
No equipment needed
Useful conditioning combo
Strong push up variation

description.en: The resistance band hip thrusts on knees is a kneeling hip thrust with band resistance. The lifter kneels on a pad with a band looped around the hips anchored behind, then thrusts the hips forward to stand tall on the knees. The band pulls back against the glutes.

en: Anchor a resistance band low to a sturdy point behind you.
Loop the band around the hips at the front of the pelvis.
Kneel on a pad with knees hip width apart.
Sit the hips back to the heels in a kneeling start.
Brace your core and squeeze the glutes.
Thrust the hips forward driving the body up to a tall kneeling position.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top against the band.
Sit back to the heels with control.
Strong glute builder
No bench needed
Trains hip extension
Builds the hamstrings
Useful glute builder
Strong band move

description.en: The resistance band Smith squat adds resistance bands to a Smith machine squat. The bands attach to the bar and anchor low, providing accommodating resistance that increases as you stand. The Smith machine fixed path eliminates balance demands while the bands force explosive drive out of the bottom.

en: Set up a Smith machine with bands attached to each end of the bar and anchored low.
Step under the bar and place it across your upper back.
Unrack the bar and step into your squat stance.
Brace your core and squat down by bending your knees and hips.
The bands should be slack at the bottom of the squat.
Drive up explosively against the increasing band tension.
Lock out at the top with hips and knees fully extended.
The bands should reach maximum tension at the top.
Accommodating resistance gets harder at lockout
Forces explosive drive out of the bottom
Smith machine fixed path eliminates balance demands
Builds lockout strength
Common method in powerlifting accessory work
Useful for breaking through squat plateaus

description.en: The reverse plank on elbows holds a face-up plank supported on the forearms with legs extended and hips elevated. It builds glute and hamstring isometric strength, opens the chest and shoulders, and strengthens the core in a posterior position.

en: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Place forearms on the floor behind you, elbows under shoulders.
Lift your hips up until your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes. Press through your forearms.
Hold for 15 to 30 seconds.
Keep your hips elevated — do not let them sag.
Look at the ceiling. Keep neck neutral.
Build up hold time progressively.
Aim for 3 to 5 holds per session.
Builds glute and hamstring isometric strength
Opens the chest and front shoulders
Develops posterior core stability
No equipment needed
Counteracts forward-rounded posture
Easier on the wrists than hand-supported reverse plank

description.en: The roll shoulder back rotation lying on floor is a thoracic mobility drill done with a foam roller under one shoulder blade. Rotating the torso while the roller stays in contact mobilizes the thoracic spine and releases the shoulder blade muscles.

en: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat.
Place a foam roller under one shoulder blade at an angle.
Cross the arms over the chest.
Brace the core and lift the hips slightly.
Rotate the torso slowly toward the working side.
Reach the top arm across the body.
Hold the rotated position briefly.
Return to start and continue for all reps then switch.
Mobilizes the thoracic spine.
Releases the shoulder blade.
Improves rotational mobility.
Useful warm-up.
Joint friendly drill.

description.en: The seated back twist is a basic spinal mobility stretch performed seated. The lifter sits tall and rotates the torso slowly to one side then the other while keeping the hips facing forward. The twist mobilizes the thoracic spine and stretches the obliques.

en: Sit tall on the floor with the legs extended forward.
Bend one leg and place the foot on the outside of the opposite knee.
Set the opposite elbow on the outside of the bent knee.
Brace your core lightly and keep the chest up.
Rotate the torso toward the bent knee side.
Use the elbow to deepen the twist.
Hold the position and breathe deeply.
Release back to center then switch sides.
Mobilizes the spine
Stretches the obliques
No equipment needed
Useful warm-up stretch
Easy to add anywhere
Strong basic stretch

description.en: The seated behind back raise is a dumbbell raise behind the body. The lifter sits on a bench with dumbbells held behind the back at the hips, then raises them up and back. The behind the back position hits the front delts in a unique stretched range.

en: Sit on the edge of a flat bench with feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand behind the body at the hips.
Brace your core and keep the chest tall.
Set the arms straight with palms facing back.
Lift the dumbbells up and back behind the body.
Continue until the arms are roughly parallel to the floor behind.
Squeeze the front delts at the top.
Lower with control to the start.
Strong front delt builder
Unique stretched range
Trains the forearms
Builds shoulder size
Useful shoulder builder
Strong dumbbell move

description.en: The side plank oblique crunch holds a side plank and brings the top knee and top elbow together in a crunching motion. It combines the static anti-lateral flexion of the side plank with dynamic oblique contraction for a complete oblique exercise.

en: Get into a side plank on your right forearm. Left hand behind your head.
Body in a straight line from heels to head.
Bring your left elbow and left knee toward each other by crunching at the waist.
Squeeze your left oblique at the crunch.
Extend back to the straight side plank position.
Continue for the desired reps.
Switch sides and repeat.
Aim for 10 to 12 reps per side.
Combines static and dynamic oblique loading
Builds oblique strength and definition
No equipment needed
Engaging side plank variation
Develops hip and shoulder stability
Useful for core development

description.en: The single leg balance cross punch combines a single leg stance with cross punches. Standing on one foot challenges balance while the punches drive rotation through the torso.

en: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Lift the opposite foot just off the floor.
Bring the hands up into a guard position.
Brace the core and engage the glute on the standing leg.
Throw a cross punch with one hand by rotating the torso.
Bring the hand back to the guard.
Throw a cross punch with the other hand.
Continue alternating for the desired duration then switch standing legs.
Builds single leg balance and core stability.
Trains rotational power through the punches.
No equipment needed.
Carryover to athletic performance.
Improves total body coordination.
Easy to scale by holding light weights.

description.en: The sled 45 degrees wide stance leg press is a leg press variation with feet placed wide on the platform. The wide stance shifts more load to the adductors and glutes while the quads still drive the press.

en: Sit in a 45 degree leg press machine with your back against the pad.
Place your feet on the platform in a wide stance with toes turned out.
Unrack the safeties and lower the platform under control.
Bend the knees toward your shoulders while keeping the lower back pinned.
Lower until your thighs nearly touch the chest or you reach end range.
Press through the heels to drive the platform back up.
Stop just before the knees lock to keep tension on the legs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Hits the adductors and inner thighs with the wide stance.
Builds glute and quad strength simultaneously.
Loads the legs without spinal compression.
Easy to load heavy with sled stability.
Trains a strong squat pattern variation.
Excellent leg builder for hypertrophy.

description.en: The sled angled single leg press is a unilateral leg press performed on the angled leg press sled. The lifter sets one foot on the platform and presses the sled up. The single leg work builds quad and glute strength symmetrically and protects the lower back.

en: Sit on an angled leg press sled with the back flat against the pad.
Place one foot on the platform centered with the hip.
Set the other foot off to the side.
Grip the handles for stability.
Brace your core and unrack the sled.
Lower the sled by bending the working knee.
Continue lowering until the knee is near the chest.
Press the sled back up to extension. Complete reps and switch legs.
Strong unilateral leg builder
Heavy load capacity
Builds the glutes
Useful for leg symmetry
Strong machine move
Builds quad size

description.en: The Smith machine hip thrust is a glute-focused hip extension exercise performed with a Smith bar across the hips while the upper back is braced against a bench. The guided bar path eliminates the need to stabilize the bar laterally, allowing you to focus entirely on squeezing the glutes. It is often easier to set up than the barbell version and allows heavier loading with less hassle.

en: Position a flat bench horizontally inside the Smith machine. Set the bar at a height that allows you to sit on the floor with the bar across your hips.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against the bench. Roll or position the Smith bar across your hip crease. Use a barbell pad for comfort.
Plant your feet hip-width apart, roughly under your knees when at the top of the thrust. Brace your core.
Twist the bar to unrack. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Continue until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. Your shins should be roughly vertical.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for one to two seconds. Do not hyperextend your lower back.
Lower your hips under control. The bar follows the guided path.
Repeat for the desired number of reps. Twist to re-rack when finished.
Guided bar path eliminates lateral stabilization demand
Allows heavy glute loading with easier setup than barbell hip thrust
Safety hooks provide built-in failure protection
Builds the glutes directly with peak contraction at the top
Easier to set up solo than barbell version
Allows easy progressive loading

description.en: The bodyweight squat is the foundational lower-body movement — sitting hips back and down to parallel or deeper, then standing back up. Mastering the bodyweight squat builds the movement pattern, hip and ankle mobility, and the foundation needed for all loaded squat variations.

en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly (5 to 15 degrees).
Extend your arms forward at shoulder height for balance, or place them at your chest.
Brace your core. Lift your chest. Look straight ahead.
Initiate the squat by sitting your hips back, then bending your knees.
Lower your body until your hip crease drops below your knees (or as deep as your mobility allows).
Keep your knees tracking over your toes. Do not let them collapse inward.
Drive through your full foot to stand. Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Foundation for all squat variations
Builds the squat movement pattern
Improves hip and ankle mobility
Builds quad, glute, and hamstring endurance
No equipment needed
Universally beneficial for all fitness levels

description.en: The suspender split fly is a TRX chest fly performed in a split (staggered) stance for added stability. The fly motion targets the chest while the staggered stance recruits the core to resist rotation. It is a great compound chest builder for home or travel.

en: Set the suspension trainer with handles at about chest height.
Stand facing away from the anchor with handles in each hand.
Step into a split stance with one foot forward.
Lean forward with arms extended to your sides at chest level.
Brace your core and keep your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest forward by spreading your arms wide.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch across the chest.
Squeeze the chest to bring the handles back together.
Builds chest strength
Engages core stabilizers
No weights required
Adjustable difficulty via foot position
Useful for home training
Trains anti-rotation core control

description.en: The v-up double crunch combines a V-up with a double crunch contraction at the top. The lifter lifts the legs and torso into a V shape, then crunches twice at the top before lowering. The double squeeze hammers the rectus abdominis hard.

en: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Brace your core hard.
Lift the legs and torso up at the same time into a V shape.
Reach the hands toward the toes at the top.
At the top crunch the body once more squeezing harder.
Pause briefly with the abs fully contracted.
Lower the legs and torso back down with control to the start.
Keep tension in the core throughout.
Strong abs builder
Doubles the contraction
Trains hip flexors
No equipment needed
Useful core finisher
Builds full core strength

description.en: The weighted Svend press (plate squeeze press) holds one or two weight plates between your palms and presses them forward by squeezing inward and pressing outward simultaneously. The squeeze activates the inner chest fibers that standard presses miss.

en: Stand tall. Hold one or two weight plates between your palms at chest height. Press your palms together firmly.
Maintain the inward squeeze throughout.
Press the plates forward by extending your arms. Keep squeezing.
Extend to full arm extension. Squeeze the inner chest hard.
Slowly pull the plates back to your chest. Maintain the squeeze.
Keep constant inward pressure throughout every rep.
Use light to moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
The squeeze is more important than the weight.
Activates the inner chest fibers
Squeeze component targets pec adduction
No bench needed
Builds chest mind-muscle connection
Easy to set up with just a plate
Excellent chest finisher
